attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The finite Schur-complement calculation is valid, but Yang-Mills input must still prove the uniform reflected Wilson boundary OPE expansion and identify H,K for the locked observable core.
steps: Lock a finite positive-time Wilson collar family and use the previously valid closed-cone argument to obtain collar-limit positivity for N_delta.

After diagonal trace continuity removes positive additive contacts, encode the remaining reflected-boundary multiplicative anomaly by widehat B_delta and test the intended target matrix q_delta=widehat N_delta oslash widehat B_delta.
Assume a uniform boundary OPE quotient expansion q_delta=E+alpha H+alpha^2K+o(alpha^2), E=11^*.
Decompose C^n=Ce plus e^perp with e=1/sqrt(n)1. The e-block of E is n, so it remains invertible for small alpha.
Compute the Schur complement on e^perp: S_delta=alpha PHP+alpha^2(PKP-(1/n)PHee^*HP)+o(alpha^2)=alpha PHP+alpha^2(PKP-n^{-2}PH11^*HP)+o(alpha^2).
Since q_delta>=0 iff the e-block is positive and S_delta>=0, a negative first-order zero-sum form or a negative corrected second-order form on ker(PHP) gives a valid finite falsifier.
Check the pure one-body case q_delta=v_delta v_delta^*: PHP=0 and PKP-n^{-2}PH11^*HP vanishes on 1^perp, confirming that the detector ignores harmless diagonal congruences.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: No current estimate controls the cutoff-to-continuum limit, collar collapse, and second-order remainder simultaneously for nonlocal Wilson hairpins at the reflection plane.

assumptions: The finite Wilson collar family has nonzero normalized boundary entries widehat B_{ij,delta} and additive positive contacts have vanished by diagonal trace continuity.
q_delta is Hermitian with diagonal one and q_delta>=0 is exactly the intended finite OS condition after the collar Schur-preimage step.
There is a scale alpha_delta>0 and Hermitian matrices H,K such that q_delta=E+alpha_delta H+alpha_delta^2 K+r_delta, E=11^*, and ||r_delta||=o(alpha_delta^2) on the finite block.
P=I-n^{-1}11^* is the orthogonal projection onto 1^perp, n is the block size, and the e=1/sqrt(n) vacuum direction has strictly positive leading eigenvalue n.
definitions: source object: regulated/collar OS matrices N_delta for a locked finite family of positive-time gauge-invariant Wilson observables, with closed-cone positivity inherited from the cutoff theory.

target object: the continuum same-theory normalized OS matrix q_delta=widehat N_delta oslash widehat B_delta obtained after removing only boundary factors already present in the locked Wilson algebra.
controlled interface: the map (widehat N_delta,widehat B_delta) -> q_delta and its expansion must be controlled for every finite reflected quadratic form in the cutoff-removal topology.

same-theory condition: diagonal Wilson normalizations may be absorbed by fixed congruence, but no boundary counterterm, pair-dependent renormalization, or enlargement of the gauge-invariant test algebra is allowed.

equations.label: same-theory Schur preimage
equations.valid_when: The boundary anomaly is multiplicative with nonzero entries and all allowed one-body factors have been locked as same-theory diagonal congruences.

equations.label: boundary OPE quotient expansion
equations.valid_when: The reflected Wilson collar OPE has a uniform finite-matrix expansion through second order in the chosen collar scale.

equations.label: first tangent gate
equations.valid_when: q_delta is positive semidefinite for all sufficiently small collars.

equations.label: second Schur gate
equations.valid_when: The first tangent gate is semidefinite and the rank-one vacuum direction is eliminated by the Schur complement.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a locked Wilson block and x in 1^perp with x^*PHPx<0, or x in ker(PHP) with x^*[PKP-n^{-2}PH11^*HP]x<0.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns the Wilson boundary OPE into a computable finite-matrix obstruction to passing reflection positivity from fixed collars to the reflection plane.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Finite Wilson collar quotient tangent-cone lemma: if the normalized same-theory Schur preimage has q_delta=11^*+alpha_delta H+alpha_delta^2 K+o(alpha_delta^2), alpha_delta downarrow 0, then valid OS positivity forces PHP>=0 on 1^perp and, on ker(PHP), P(K-n^{-2}H11^*H)P>=0. A negative value is a finite same-theory falsifier.

assumptions: q_delta is rank one through second order, representing only individual Wilson-loop collar factors.
H=a1^*+1a^* and K=b1^*+1b^*+aa^* on the finite block.
definitions: A pure one-body quotient has q_delta=v_delta v_delta^* with v_delta=1+alpha_delta a+alpha_delta^2 b+o(alpha_delta^2), possibly after harmless diagonal congruence.
The mixed detector is the quadratic form L=P K P-n^{-2}P H11^*H P on 1^perp.
The cancellation is normalization-safe because P1=0 and the vacuum Schur correction exactly subtracts |a^*x|^2.

equations.label: rank-one expansion
equations.valid_when: The boundary factor is purely one-body and no mixed reflected Wilson OPE term is present.

equations.label: one-body second-order cancellation
equations.valid_when: The expansion above holds and x is a zero-sum test vector.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the corrected form is negative after this cancellation, it cannot be explained by a one-body Wilson renormalization.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Separates removable Wilson normalizations from real mixed boundary obstructions.
candidate_lemmas.statement: One-body cancellation lemma: a pure diagonal/rank-one Wilson boundary renormalization is invisible to the corrected second-order tangent test; hence a negative corrected K-form detects a genuine mixed boundary anomaly.

falsifier: PHP>=0 but some x in ker(PHP) has x^*[PKP-n^{-2}PH11^*HP]x<0; this is the corrected second-order mixed boundary obstruction.
falsifier: collar remainders contain uncontrolled alpha^2 log alpha or cutoff/collar cross-terms, so the stated tangent expansion is not valid for the RG topology.
falsifier: widehat B_delta has zeros or requires a pair-dependent boundary counterterm; then the Schur preimage is not a same-theory operation.
falsifier: the locked gauge-invariant Wilson core is not stable under the reflected boundary OPE, so the matrix being tested belongs to a different theory.
